Independent C++ enumeration of all 4^(2n) labelings for n=3,4,5, with all k=1,...,3n, matched exactly two exceptions and each predicted remaining optimum.
correctness.rationale: Cr_n has closed neighborhoods of size n. Summing their >=k inequalities proves W>=2k. In equality all are tight, and paired labels obey x_i-y_i=c, (n-2)c=0, hence x_i=y_i=z_i with sum z_i=k. The given integer-count vector constructions include a value 3 (or a 2) to defend all relevant labels and attain W=2k unless n+k=5; exactly (3,2) and (4,1) fail the requisite rescue. A paired shore-difference parity analysis rules out W=2k+1 for those cases; vectors (-1,1,3) and (-1,-1,1,3) duplicated attain 2k+2. Exhaustively checked every f in {-1,1,2,3}^{2n} for n=3,4,5 and all 3n admissible k with an independent C++ implementation. No finite test is used for the all-n assertion.
residual_risks: Not a theorem for arbitrary deleted matchings or nonpositive k.
